newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO chief declines to comment on Lebed sacking.
newsitem.headline: NATO chief declines to comment on Lebed sacking.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana declined to comment on Thursday's sacking by President Boris Yeltsin of Alexander Lebed as Russia's security supremo.
"I have no comment at all to make," a smiling Solana, who only last week hosted Lebed at NATO's political headquarters in Brussels, told reporters.

Solana, who was escorting Slovakian President Michal Kovac to NATO's main exit after a routine courtesy visit, would not be drawn on whether Lebed's ouster would have any impact on NATO's plans for eastward expansion.

Kovac said he saw no reason why the sacking of Lebed and the generally uncertain situation in Russia should accelerate or slow the process of NATO taking in new members from former communist central and eastern Europe.

"This is the Russians sorting out their own leadership problems," said one senior diplomat. "You can even argue that Yeltsin taking action is better than allowing the power struggle to keep going on".
Yeltsin brought Lebed into his team after the reserve general scored a strong 15 percent in the first round of Russia's presidential election.
But Lebed has won few friends in the Kremlin and Interior Ministry Anatoly Kulikov on Wednesday accused him of plotting a "creeping coup" and trying to seize power. Lebed denied the charges.

After Lebed's visit, his first to the West, NATO sources said the alliance felt it had found someone with whom it could do business and said they hoped he would take over responsibility for NATO enlargement and NATO-Russia relations.
Moscow opposes the alliance's enlargement plans, saying the organisation was a product of the Cold War.
In Brussels, Lebed moderated his previous outbursts against the alliance and said he saw many areas for cooperation.
